source_refs.note: Exercise 3.5, Question 7: integral of f from f(x) + f(-x); book p. 102. Key on p. 300 under 'Exercise 3.2' (8/3). The printed condition x^2 + x^3 is impossible; corrected to x^2.

blocks.text: As printed: Let \(f(x)\) be a function satisfying \(f(x) + f(-x) = x^2 + x^3\) for all \(x\). Evaluate the definite integral \(\int_{-2}^{2} f(x)\,dx\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: No function can satisfy \(f(x) + f(-x) = x^2 + x^3\) for all \(x\): replacing \(x\) by \(-x\) leaves the left side unchanged but turns the right side into \(x^2 - x^3\), so we would need \(x^3 = 0\) for every \(x\). (At \(x = 1\) the condition says \(f(1) + f(-1) = 2\), at \(x = -1\) it says \(f(-1) + f(1) = 0\).) Because the left side is always even, only the even part \(x^2\) can be meant: \(f(x) + f(-x) = x^2\) (for example \(f(x) = \frac{x^2}{2} + x^3\)). With it the answer is \(\frac{8}{3}\), the key's value. With the printed data two correct methods give different results (\(\frac{8}{3}\) and \(\frac{20}{3}\)), which shows the data are inconsistent.

blocks.prompt: 7 Let \(f(x)\) be a function satisfying \(f(x) + f(-x) = x^2\) [printed as \(x^2 + x^3\); see the correction above] for all \(x\). Evaluate the definite integral \(\int_{-2}^{2} f(x)\,dx\).
blocks.explanation:
We know only \(f(x) + f(-x)\), not \(f\) itself, and the interval \([-2, 2]\) is symmetric.
Property V turns \(\int_{-a}^{a} f\) into \(\int_0^a [f(x) + f(-x)]\,dx\), which uses exactly what is given.
We use the condition \(f(x) + f(-x) = x^2\) (see the correction above).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) + f(-x) = x^2\) for all \(x\) (printed \(x^2 + x^3\)).
To find: \(\int_{-2}^{2} f(x)\,dx\).
Method: Property V \(\int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{a} \big(f(x) + f(-x)\big)\,dx\) with \(a = 2\).

Why the printed condition must be corrected
\[x \to -x:\ f(-x) + f(x) = x^2 - x^3\]
\[\Rightarrow\ x^2 + x^3 = x^2 - x^3\]
Why: the left side \(f(x) + f(-x)\) does not change when \(x\) becomes \(-x\), so the right side must not change either; \(x^3\) does change, so it cannot be part of a true condition.

Apply Property V
\[\int_{-2}^{2} f(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{2} \big(f(x) + f(-x)\big)\,dx\]
\[= \int_{0}^{2} x^2\,dx\]
Why: put in the given (corrected) condition.

Second method (the one the key follows)
\[I = \int_{-2}^{2} f(-x)\,dx\]
\[2I = \int_{-2}^{2} \big(f(x) + f(-x)\big)\,dx\]
\[= \int_{-2}^{2} x^2\,dx = \dfrac{16}{3},\quad I = \dfrac{8}{3}\]
Why: Property IV(ii) with \(b = 2\) lets us replace \(x\) by \(-x\). With the printed \(x^2 + x^3\) this method still gives \(\frac{8}{3}\) (because \(\int_{-2}^{2} x^3\,dx = 0\)), but Property V would give \(\int_0^2 (x^2 + x^3)\,dx = \frac{20}{3}\); two different answers prove the printed data are impossible.

Check with an example
\[f(x) = \dfrac{x^2}{2} + x^3:\ f(x) + f(-x) = x^2\]
\[\int_{-2}^{2} \left(\dfrac{x^2}{2} + x^3\right)dx = \dfrac{8}{3} + 0 \;\checkmark\]
Why: a concrete function satisfying the corrected condition gives the same value. The key prints \(\frac{8}{3}\).
